text:
emma: Customer observed duplicate charge when a 429 happened right as the SDK did a token refresh. Logs show an immediate retry plus the queued retry after refresh.

alex: sounds like a race: SDK retried while refresh in-flight. Do we have a repro?

emma: short log:
```
09:01:00 INFO req id=zzz status=429 retry-after=0.3
09:01:00 INFO auth refresh start
09:01:00 INFO req id=zzz immediate retry -> 200 (side-effect)
09:01:01 INFO auth refresh done; queued retry -> 200 (side-effect)
```

vikram: root cause identified. Quick fixes: 1) SDKs should default to queueing mutates while refresh is in-flight, 2) sample apps should send Idempotency-Key by default for writes, 3) respect Retry-After and add jittered backoff for 429 immediate retries.

nate: parity note: Py currently behaves differently (queues by default) so Node needs alignment.

alex: proposal: when refresh in-progress, enqueue unless request has explicit Idempotency-Key (then allow immediate send). Add client flag `allow_immediate_replay` to opt-out. Backoff formula: delay = base * (2^attempt) * (0.75 + rand()*0.5). Always honor Retry-After if > 0.9s.

emma: tests: add an integration that mocks 429 -> auth refresh -> server accepts both replays, assert only one side-effect in final state. Also add telemetry: sdk.replay.during_refresh.count.

vikram: I'll update sampleapp to set Idempotency-Key and add an e2e. nate take the Node SDK queueing + metric. alex please review RFC when drafted.

docs-bot: RFC draft created: "auth-refresh-replay-race" link tbd.

emma: timeline: patch for Node next week, Py parity after. Document behavior for streaming as follow-up.

alex: add code comments in both SDKs explaining queue rationale. Good catch everyone.
